name: Electro-osmotic wound dressing
subtitle: a flat dressing that drains wounds without suction

effects.effect: a voltage across a wet porous material makes the liquid flow

effect: a voltage across a wet porous material makes the liquid flow
how: Deep and diabetic wounds heal faster when their fluid is drawn off, but today that takes a suction pump on a hose that patients carry everywhere. This thin dressing holds a porous layer between two mesh electrodes; a coin-cell voltage pulls the wound fluid up through the pores (electro-osmosis) into an absorbent pad, silently and with no airtight seal to leak.
obstacle: Wound fluid is salty and full of protein, which slows the flow and clogs the pores within days.
why: Chronic wounds cost limbs and lives; a silent flat dressing could replace a suction machine.
real: US patent 8353928 ('Electrochemical wound therapy') claims electro-osmotically moving wound fluid from a cavity over the wound into a chamber/sponge; no clinical or prototype demonstration found.
